name: Acadiana Plastics Molding
old_description: Acadiana Plastics Molding thrives on innovation and unparalleled customer satisfaction.
about:
Acadiana Plastics Molding operates from New Iberia, Louisiana, where it was founded in 1989 by Kent Byron. The company remains locally owned and operated, with Byron serving as president and chief executive officer. What began as a three-person venture aimed at filling a regional gap—Louisiana food producers previously had to source injection-molded closures from out of state—has grown into a nearly 100-employee operation.

The 22-acre facility houses injection molding presses ranging from 60 to 500 tons, capable of producing parts from 0.05 grams to over 1,000 grams. Annual output exceeds 500 million closures in sizes from 10 mm to 48 mm, including continuous-thread and tamper-evident styles with custom lining options. The product line also covers 19 standard PET bottle styles and the patented STAT® Vial, a unit-dose heat-seal package for the respiratory market, supported by an in-house vial printing process. Engineering and design consulting are offered alongside molding.

Primary markets include the pepper sauce and condiment sector, where the company says it dominates closure sales, as well as respiratory pharmaceutical packaging and craft beverage brands seeking custom containers.

Byron started the business after recognizing that no Southern Louisiana shop specialized in injection-molded plastic closures, forcing local food manufacturers to look elsewhere. The company emphasizes a partnership-oriented service model rather than a purely transactional one, a philosophy it traces back to its founding vision.

name: Accumold
old_description: Bring your ideal micro part design and let Accumold be your key to success.
about:
Accumold operates from a 15-acre campus in Ankeny, Iowa, just north of Des Moines. The company traces its roots to a rented garage where its founders recognized a growing demand for micro injection molded components that exceeded the capabilities of conventional molding systems. While the exact founding year is not publicly stated, the firm notes four decades of exclusive focus on micro molding and tooling.

Accumold provides vertically integrated micro manufacturing, encompassing tooling, injection molding, micro 3D printing, packaging, and metrology under one roof. Its core process is high-precision thermoplastic injection molding for parts with micron-level tolerances, complemented by additive manufacturing for rapid prototyping. The campus houses advanced metrology including a Zygo NewView 8300 optical profiler, OGP multi-sensor systems, and Keyence vision inspection, enabling measurement of features down to tenths of a micron. The company also offers design for micro molding (DfMM), process validation, and Gage R&R studies.

Materials range from medical-grade biocompatible resins (ISO 10993) to engineering thermoplastics such as ABS, PVC, PMMA, and nylon equivalents.

Accumold differentiates itself by embedding metrology into every production stage, asserting that "if you cannot measure it, you cannot make it." Its vertically integrated model ensures that tooling, molding, and inspection are co-located, allowing rapid iteration and consistent quality at micro scale. The firm emphasizes continuous investment in measurement technology and automation to maintain precision as parts shrink further.

Accusemble Electronics Inc. was founded in 1979 and operates from North Billerica, Massachusetts. The company is led by President Deborah Bayley and has built its reputation on the principles of quality, value, and service.

The company provides custom circuit board assembly and contract manufacturing services ranging from engineering prototypes and new product introduction (NPI) through low-, medium-, and high-volume production runs. Its capabilities include surface-mount technology (SMT) assembly using five Yamaha pick-and-place systems, automated optical and X-ray inspection, drag soldering and hybrid heating rework stations, conformal coating with urethane and acrylic materials, and full supply-chain procurement. The facility also offers extensive rework and repair services for electronic assemblies.

Accusemble serves both defense and commercial markets. In the defense sector it delivers mission-critical circuit board assemblies built to rigorous standards. Commercial customers span consumer electronics and industrial applications, where the company supplies custom, high-quality circuit board solutions.

The business was started to provide high-quality contract manufacturing with a focus on continual improvement of manufacturing methods. President Deborah Bayley states that the company maintains a constant desire to offer products and services of superior quality and workmanship, supported by an in-house IPC-A-610-certified trainer and advanced inspection technology.

name: Advanced Circuitry International
old_description: At Advanced Circuitry International we’ve been manufacturing a wide array of Antenna PCB’s since 2011.
about:
Advanced Circuitry International was founded in 1992 in Duluth, Georgia, as an independently owned manufacturer of high-reliability RF/microwave and antenna printed circuit boards. The company began with a focus on aerospace, defense, telecommunications, and medical device markets, building expertise in exotic substrates such as Teflon and ceramics.

Today the company operates a 70,000-square-foot facility and is expanding into an additional 50,000 square feet. Its capabilities span RF/microwave PCBs, antenna PCBs, large-format boards up to 24 by 102 inches, multilayer constructions, rapid prototyping, and full assembly of RF/microwave and antenna sub-systems. The shop also provides design-for-manufacturability assistance, impedance modeling, in-process and final inspection testing, and a logistics program that stocks laminate materials and finished goods for qualified customers.

Advanced Circuitry serves a global base of OEMs and EMS providers across land, sea, air, and space applications. Specific markets include 5G infrastructure, base stations, GPS, microwave communications, small cells, automotive electronics, and marine systems. The company's customer list includes notable original equipment manufacturers and electronics manufacturing services firms worldwide.

It emphasizes control of passive intermodulation (PIM) for low-PIM applications, rapid turnaround supported by a large inventory of RF materials, and the ability to produce exceptionally large antenna structures on a wide range of high-frequency laminates.

Target markets include medical, clinical, research, commercial, and industrial sectors, with the company noting that its intellectual property can extend into other large vertical markets. Customers range from hospitals and research labs to commercial and industrial operators seeking compact, energy‑efficient devices.

Advanced Medical Device Technologies was founded to provide technologies that enhance patient outcomes by improving safety, reducing costs, and increasing reliability. The company emphasizes "breakthrough thinking and agile collaboration," aiming to engineer quality in and costs out through advanced technology and streamlined manufacturing. Its differentiators include in-house automation, a broad press range, and end-to-end services from concept to global delivery.

name: AeroLEDs, LLC
about:
AeroLEDs, LLC is based in Boise, Idaho, and was founded in 2006 with a mission to redefine modern LED aerospace lighting. The company entered a market that had seen little change in 50 years and introduced the first LED-based airplane lights, raising the bar for performance and quality.

The company designs and manufactures a range of LED lighting solutions for aircraft, including wingtip and tail lights, landing, taxi, and recognition lights, and beacons. It also produces specialized experimental lighting and STC‑approved LED kits for jets and turboprops. Manufacturing processes include aluminum heat‑sink fabrication with black powder coating and integrated lighting‑system assembly. Installations span experimental and Part 23 aircraft through to space and military programs, with products fielded on over 15 tactical military platforms.

AeroLEDs serves the general aviation, business jet, turboprop, military, and space sectors. Its customer base includes experimental aircraft builders (notably the Vans RV community), operators of certified jets and turboprops, and military programs requiring both overt and covert lighting solutions.

The business was started because the aerospace lighting market was stagnant and in drastic need of a new product with a fresh look and unequaled performance. By creating the first LED‑based airplane lights, AeroLEDs forced legacy manufacturers to respond and moved aircraft lighting from a forgotten necessity to a desired accessory.

about:
Alabama Chanin operates from Florence, Alabama, where it began in 2000 with a documentary film titled Stitch and 200 hand-crafted T-shirts made by artisans in the Shoals region. The organization formally established as Alabama Chanin in 2006 and now functions as a 501(c)(3) nonprofit under Project Threadways, a single not-for-profit entity that also encompasses The School of Making and arts and humanities programs.

The company designs and produces textiles by hand, specializing in artisan-led clothing and made-to-order pieces crafted from organic cotton fabrics using slow, intentional methods. A new headquarters and community space, The Maker Lab broke ground in January 2026 to house studios, workshop rooms, exhibitions, a café, and retail. The organization also publishes books, kits, and patterns, and runs workshops teaching sewing, embroidery, and design exploration for over 100 participants per session.

Alabama Chanin serves direct consumers purchasing high-end garments (priced from $698 to $2,858), craft-education participants, and attendees of its Project Threadways symposiums on sustainability and textile culture. Past collaborations include a long-standing partnership with Heath Ceramics beginning in 2011, and a pandemic pivot to producing face masks in 2020. Its archive preserves two decades of oral histories, oral history interviews, and public history projects.

The enterprise was founded on the belief that making holds power—emphasizing transparent supply chains, ethical labor, cultural heritage preservation, and creative placemaking. Its mission integrates production, education, and documentation to sustain artisan craft and keep continuity between makers, materials, and place.

The primary customer base is Southeast Alaska's commercial fishing fleet, which operates from California to the Aleutian Islands. ACE also serves onshore industrial clients, including municipal water and wastewater utilities, power generation facilities, and remote telecommunications sites.

The company emphasizes that reliable equipment and timely repair are critical during short fishing openings and hostile conditions. name: Albuquerque Fashion Incubator
old_description: The Albuquerque Fashion Incubator offers a one-of-a-kind, hands-on training opportunity in sewn product manufacturing. It is the only one of its kind in the world. Really.
about:
Albuquerque Fashion Incubator (ABQFI) operates from Albuquerque, New Mexico, where it has hosted apparel manufacturing boot camps since 2015. Organized as a 501(c)3 non-profit, ABQFI began with a single “Coats for Kids” event and now runs two annual cycles of pre-production and production camps at the Albuquerque Sewing Factory on Old Coors Drive.

The incubator’s core activity is a four-day, hands-on boot camp that takes participants through the full sewn-product manufacturing process: pattern creation, production pattern auditing, work-instruction development, fabric spreading, cutting, sewing, and finishing. Each cycle includes a pre-production camp roughly three months before the production camp; attendees who register for pre-production are automatically enrolled in the production phase. Camps are capped at 25 participants, and the inaugural event produced 125 fully lined winter coats in four days using industrial equipment at the factory.

The training targets entrepreneurs, aspiring designers, and individuals with no prior factory experience—75 percent of the first cohort had never used an industrial machine. The program also offers custom boot camps for larger groups by arrangement.

Fasanella launched the incubator to address the loss of domestic production knowledge, arguing that re-shoring requires people who know how to run factories. The model combines free instruction (participants cover only material costs) with charitable output, positioning ABQFI as a unique workforce-development and community-service hybrid.

old_description: Radiation-hardened, high-performance power solutions built for space, defense, and the harshest environments on Earth.
about:
Apogee Semiconductor was founded in 2017 in Plano, Texas, launched with a National Science Foundation grant to solve the reliability problem of commercial off-the-shelf (COTS) components in space and defense applications. The founding team established the company as a U.S.-based supplier of radiation-hardened power, analog, and mixed-signal integrated circuits.

The company designs fault-containment ICs that serve as a protective architecture layer around COTS parts, rather than replacing every component. Its product portfolio includes radiation-hardened shift registers, I/O expanders, smart high-side power switches, level translators, majority voters, and GPIO expanders. Apogee operates a fabless model, partnering with qualified foundry, assembly, and test suppliers while maintaining oversight through documented processes and traceability. By 2022 the company had shipped 10,000 units, and its components achieved verified flight heritage in 2023.

Its components have been validated through NASA's Tipping Point program and are used in mission-critical power architectures where deterministic fault containment and telemetry are required.

Apogee differentiates itself by building fault containment into the silicon architecture rather than screening commercial parts after fabrication. The company's Zero-Power-Penalty™ cold-sparing technology eliminates leakage current in redundant circuits, and its LEO and GEO product variants share identical form, fit, and function to simplify design reuse. Apogee emphasizes engineer-to-engineer support, publishing all test data openly and responding to technical inquiries within 24 hours.

Thompson brings over 40 years of automotive repair experience and holds 27 U.S. and international patents, while Pederson’s background includes control systems for national laboratories and high-tech industries. The company began as a developer of patented diagnostic tools for the automotive sector.

The company manufactures a range of diagnostic equipment including multi-channel oscilloscopes (eSCOPE series), OBD II drivability scan tools (eSCAN), misfire detectors, pressure transducers, vibration analyzers, leak detectors, gas analyzers, borescopes, engine simulators, ignition analyzers, and training products. Electronic and software design is supported through its affiliate VI Control Systems, which has developed controls for lasers, particle accelerators, and nuclear reactors.

The company’s tools have been recognized with awards from Motor Magazine, TST, Undercar Digest, Transmission Digest, and the Mobile Air Conditioning Society spanning 2004 through 2021.

The founders’ combined expertise in automotive repair and advanced control systems drives the company’s focus on patented, award-winning solutions that translate complex vehicle data into actionable diagnostics for technicians of any skill level.

about:
Axon Circuit, Inc. is a printed circuit board manufacturer headquartered in Tampa, Florida. The company was founded in 1990 and has operated continuously in the Southeast United States for over three decades.

The firm produces rigid PCBs ranging from single-sided and double-sided boards to multilayer constructions up to 16 layers. Its capabilities include fine-line and surface-mount technology pitches, board thicknesses from 0.008 to 0.250 inches, carbon ink contacts, oversized multilayer panels, ball grid array patterns, blind and buried vias, peelable and water-soluble masks, plated slots and edges, epoxy via plug, and controlled impedance. Surface finishes offered are solder mask over bare copper, hot air solder leveling, electroless nickel/gold (including bondable gold), electroless white tin, electroless silver, screenable silver and carbon, and heavy copper layers. The 25,000-square-foot facility employs more than 40 people and has produced over 100 million rigid PCBs, with annual revenue exceeding $5 million. The company owns its equipment and recently invested over $1 million in new fabrication and testing systems.

Axon Circuit serves customers in communications, instrumentation and controls, consumer electronics, medical devices, automotive, and military sectors. Its clientele is primarily business-to-business, built largely through referrals.

The company emphasizes an attitude of continuous improvement, personalized service, and on-time delivery. It maintains a supplier performance guarantee, offers competitive domestic and offshore quotes, and operates an internal waste treatment and reverse osmosis system to reduce environmental impact.

The firm differentiates itself through full vertical integration, which shortens lead times and tightens supply-chain control; a 90-percent on-time delivery record; real-time quality tracking via SAP; and a family culture that prioritizes long-term customer relationships over transactional sales.

Formed as a 501(c)(6) nonprofit under the Medical Center of the Americas Foundation, it was established to strengthen the medical device sector spanning the U.S.–Mexico border. A board led by Chair Julio Chiu and Vice Chair Mylena Walker governs the initiative, which formally links the Medical Center of the Americas Foundation with the Clúster Biomédico de Juárez.

The organization does not manufacture products. Instead, it convenes manufacturers, government agencies, academic institutions, and nonprofits to develop regional capabilities, map supply-chain competencies, and monitor cluster growth. Its programs create collaborative networks, promote the region’s biomedical ecosystem globally, and leverage the strategic El Paso–Juárez location to optimize cost, efficiency, and quality for member companies.

By connecting these entities across boundaries, the cluster aims to accelerate the formation, expansion, and retention of biomedical enterprises while improving healthcare quality in the region.

about:
BUILT is a custom millwork and cabinetry firm based in Tampa, Florida. Founded in 2013 by Andrew Watson, the company began as a one-man operation with a few tools and a credit card, driven by a passion for making. Over more than a decade, it has grown into a dedicated in-house team serving refined residential projects throughout the state.

The shop produces architectural millwork — wall paneling, libraries, built-ins, ceiling details, and integrated trim — along with custom cabinetry for kitchens, dressing rooms, vanities, bars, and wine rooms. It also builds bespoke furniture and executes commercial and hospitality interiors such as restaurant bars and reception desks. Every project is engineered, fabricated, finished, and installed by the company's own crew, using 3D modeling to resolve conflicts before cutting and advanced fabrication capability paired with hand-finished craftsmanship.

BUILT works primarily with interior designers, architects, general contractors, and developers on complex, high-budget residences, as well as directly with discerning homeowners.

Watson started BUILT to bridge the gap between small studio craftsmanship and factory-scale reliability, delivering the precision expected in premium homes with the project management discipline required by professional design teams. The firm emphasizes structured scheduling, in-house control of all phases, and detailing engineered for Gulf Coast humidity.

The company differentiates itself by documenting the provenance of each timber source—such as floorboards from the Meadow River Lumber Company, once the world's largest sawmill—and passing those stories to the buyer. The "Always Home" brand promise underscores a commitment to warmth, craftsmanship, and West Virginia heritage.

about:
Benchmark’s Huntsville operation sits in the heart of Alabama’s Rocket City The site traces its manufacturing lineage to 1963, when the facility began serving the region’s emerging aerospace and defense sectors.

The plant provides end-to-end electronics manufacturing and engineering services. Its advanced manufacturing floor handles mechanical and precision machining, microelectronics, mixed and hybrid assembly, PCB assembly and surface-mount technology, and full system build and integration. Engineering teams deliver electrical, mechanical, and microwave/millimeter-wave design, software development, test development, and design-for-excellence support. The site also runs automation solutions, environmental stress screening, and mmWave test capabilities, backed by lifecycle management services including depot repair, sustaining engineering, and supply chain management.

Customers span commercial aerospace, defense, advanced computing, medical technologies, industrial, next-gen communications, and semiconductor capital equipment. The Huntsville team has built UAV communications modules and flight computers for FAA-regulated programs, scaled high-volume lidar sensor production for Ouster, delivered AI-enabled mobile surveillance systems for U.S. Customs and Border Protection, and manufactured components for Intel’s Aurora exascale supercomputer and HPE’s AI infrastructure. Other projects include autonomous mobile robot redesigns, satellite communication terminal transfers, and cryogenic kiosks for stem cell therapy.

Benchmark emphasizes its Buy American and TAA-compliant solutions, a workforce with an average 15-year tenure, and close collaboration with the company’s Minnesota and Santa Ana design centers. The site maintains ITAR registration and AS9100 certification to meet defense and aerospace requirements.

about:
Big Picture Foods operates from Barrington, Rhode Island, producing a line of artisan specialty foods centered on regeneratively farmed organic olives. The company emphasizes small-batch craft production, with olives that are sun-ripened and hand-picked at peak perfection before undergoing a natural fermentation process.

The product range includes several olive varieties—such as Greek Mix, Green Amfissa, and Double Stuffed Garlic & Jalapeño—alongside wild foraged capers, extra virgin olive oil, and jarred banana and red peppers. All items are slow-cured using natural fermentation, which the company says preserves nutrients and yields gut-friendly probiotics. Every product contains only four ingredients and no additives or preservatives.

Big Picture Foods sells through a growing network of retail partners across the United States, directing consumers to a store locator on its website. The brand targets shoppers seeking raw, antioxidant-rich pantry staples that support digestive health and anti-inflammatory benefits, positioning itself as an alternative to chemically cured, mass-produced equivalents.

The company frames its mission around regenerative agriculture, stating that its groves withdrew 20 tons of carbon from the atmosphere last year compared with seven tons added by conventional methods. It describes this climate impact as core to its "different bottom line," linking soil health directly to the flavor and nutritional profile of its fermented foods.

Black Diamond Woodworks LLC operates from Bozeman, Montana, serving the Gallatin Valley. The company brings over 30 years of construction and carpentry experience and has been a registered independent contractor for more than 15 years.

Black Diamond Woodworks distinguishes itself with a choice of cost-plus-percentage-fee or fixed-price bidding, a fully insured operation, and an emphasis on clear communication and organized project management. The team’s deep experience in both structural and finish carpentry allows them to handle projects from initial framing through final millwork installation.

Blackhawk Molding Co operates from Mayflower, Arkansas, where it has built over 75 years of capping excellence. The company specializes in injection molding of closures for the dairy, juice, and water industries, producing tamper-evident caps and offering assembly, closure decoration, and label production. Its capabilities include an in-house toolroom, design and development of value-added packaging, and a technical service team that conducts preliminary surveys, bottle blowing for neck sizing, equipment auditing, and conversion assistance. Blackhawk markets itself as the world's provider of 55 mm closures.

Primary customers are bottlers in the dairy, juice, water, and broader beverage sectors. The technical team works directly with blow-mold operators and equipment vendors to ensure proper neck finishes and cap performance, serving both new and existing accounts.

Blackhawk emphasizes environmental sustainability through lightweight caps that reduce resin consumption and the SafeGard Plus cap, which incorporates calcium carbonate as a resin additive to cut plastic waste. The company also highlights its family-oriented culture and intellectual property development as differentiators.

name: Blazer Electric Supply Company Colorado Springs
about:
Blazer Electric Supply operates from Colorado Springs, Colorado. The current incarnation of the company was established in 2009 by Mike and Steve Blazer, who had originally founded the business in 1984 alongside their brother Fred. That first venture grew into the largest electrical distributor in Southern Colorado before being sold in 1999. A decade later, the Blazer brothers re-entered the market with 30 former employees and rebuilt the operation.

Today the company functions as a wholesale electrical distributor, stocking roughly $5 million of inventory across an 83,000-square-foot warehouse served by more than 90 associates. Beyond standard product distribution — spanning categories such as conduit, wire, lighting, control automation, and renewable-energy components — Blazer provides job-site services including storage containers, inventory management, and project staging. A dedicated ProFab department offers laser engraving, while a rental fleet and after-hours delivery (Night Strike) and 24/7 express pickup (Beep & Beep) round out the service portfolio.

Its product lines cover data and telecom, power distribution, fire alarm, and safety equipment, reflecting the needs of commercial and industrial projects.

Blazer emphasizes its independence as a locally owned operation, arguing that this structure enables faster decision-making and tailored service. The company points to a string of industry awards — including multiple IMARK Distributor of the Year honors and a second-place ranking in a national customer-satisfaction survey of over 50 distributors — as evidence of its service focus.

about:
Blissmade Furniture Co. operates from Dunbarton, New Hampshire, where it designs and builds heirloom furniture and cabinetry. The company focuses on premium native hardwoods and traditional joinery techniques inspired by early American timber frames and cabins.

The product line spans six distinct collections—Bay Point, Early American, Galehead, Studio Craft, Lakehouse, and Shaker Harvest—each drawing on historical American furniture styles. In addition to case goods, the company reproduces solid brass hardware using traditional patterns. Production relies on hand-fitted joinery and solid-wood construction rather than veneers or particle board.

The collections are marketed as heirloom-grade furnishings built to withstand seasonal changes and generations of use.

The company emphasizes the simplicity and durability of traditional joinery as its defining aesthetic, positioning each piece as a modern continuation of early American craft traditions.
